task.title: Page one-shot schedule inventory
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/987 with bounded exact-ID keyset paging over authoritative one-shot schedule streams.
acceptance_criteria: Validate a positive at-most-1024 page size and return complete schedules in exact-ID order.
Use an optional exclusive exact-ID cursor and expose continuation only after validating one lookahead stream.
Fail closed on selected evidence while isolating corruption before the cursor or beyond lookahead.

attempts.diagnostic: Paging tests failed because SchedulePageSize, SchedulePage, and ScheduleStore::list_page did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added focused tests for size bounds, ordering, continuation, nonexistent cursors, empty and read-only behavior, unrelated streams, and corruption windows.

attempts.summary: Implemented and refactored the bounded kernel slice.
attempts.diagnostic: Implemented bounded authoritative-stream keyset selection with one validated lookahead and canonical complete schedule replay.
attempts.patch: Implemented issue 987 in crates/vela-kernel/src/scheduler.rs with focused store tests, ADR-0093, and scheduler documentation.

attempts.diagnostic: Independent review found no blocking issues; a rate-limited false green was excluded until genuine CodeRabbit run dca27617 completed on the exact head with no actionable comments and zero unresolved threads.
attempts.patch: Preserved the exact verified head through cooldown before enabling squash merge.

outcome.summary: Issue 987 delivered bounded one-shot schedule inventory paging without changing durable event schemas or lifecycle authority.

verification.command: GitHub Rust quality gate for pull request 988 exact head 309fee817aadb233ccd50ce63df85af5fd92478b

lessons: Existing exact schedule IDs are sufficient for stable keyset continuation without persisted cursor state.
Selected lookahead corruption must block misleading continuation while out-of-window corruption remains isolated.
Status or due paging requires a separate bounded sparse-selection contract; this slice adds no mutation, dispatch, or execution authority.
